Devin (Acme Product): hey team — our app just got a bunch of 429s and the dashboard shows 'monthly credits exhausted'. we thought we had more remaining; can someone confirm when monthly credits actually reset?

Maya (Support): sorry for the trouble, Devin. quick answers first: monthly credits/quotas reset at the start of your billing cycle. for standard monthly accounts that’s 00:05 UTC on the first day of your billing month. if you signed up mid-month or have a custom billing anchor, your reset aligns with the account’s billing anchor date, not necessarily calendar month.

Devin (Acme Product): we signed up on Feb 12th — so should it have reset on Mar 12th at 00:05 UTC? our product metrics show heavy usage on Mar 11th but the dashboard showed exhausted hours earlier in the day.

Maya (Support): yes, if your billing anchor is Feb 12th the quota window is anchored to that date. can you share the account id or customer email? I can check the exact anchor and the reset job run time. also: there’s a scheduled reset job that runs at ~00:00-00:10 UTC; on rare occasions the finalization/freeze of usage ledgers completes a few minutes later which can make the visible dashboard update lag by a small amount.

Devin (Acme Product): account is acme@acme.com, acct id: acct_01GxQp. the dashboard update lag seems bigger tho — it showed exhausted at 08:40 UTC and we only had sustained traffic earlier that morning for a few minutes.

Maya (Support): thanks. i pulled the ledger: the monthly credit bucket did reset at 2026-03-12T00:05:21Z for your billing anchor, but there are two things that could explain what you saw: 1) token metering — some calls (embeddings + large generations) are charged as they complete, so if you had a backlog/slow responses, completion times pushed token accounting into later windows; 2) overage protection and emergency fallback — when a monthly bucket is exhausted, the system will attempt fallback ordering (reserved capacity, trial credits, or block) depending on your account policy, and the UI shows a transition state while that policy is evaluated.

Devin (Acme Product): hmm we didn’t expect completion-time accounting. can you explain how that shows up in logs or headers? i want to reproduce for our engineering team.

Anika (SE): quick repro steps we share with customers: 1) run a large-generation request that takes a few seconds (e.g., long completion for chat with 2k+ output tokens); 2) immediately after sending, poll usage endpoints to see pre-completion counters; 3) check request logs for the finalization event and compare token usage timestamp. in the request logs you’ll see request_id + final token count when the response stream finishes. also look at X-Request-Id in server logs and the usage audit entry (we log usage entries when we finalize billing for that request).

Maya (Support): example: curl + show usage entry snippet — we log something like:

```
POST /v1/chat/completions
Request-Id: req_0a1b2c
...<body truncated>

// later in usage audit table (time is completion_time)
{ "account": "acct_01GxQp", "request_id": "req_0a1b2c", "tokens": 4321, "charged_at": "2026-03-12T08:39:55Z" }
```

Maya (Support): if charged_at is after midnight in your case that could cause the bucket to look exhausted at 08:40 even if the request started earlier.

Devin (Acme Product): makes sense. is there any grace behavior for customers who go over a monthly credit unexpectedly? we had an important run and customers were blocked.

Tom (Billing): normally we block on exhaustion unless a customer has overage enabled or active trial/top-up. we do have a short emergency grace flow for enterprise / Dedicated customers that can be enabled: automatic temporary soft-cap so a few critical requests can complete while the billing collector alerts the team. for your account I see no overage permission enabled. we can offer a manual top-up or temporary extension — do you want us to apply a one-off credit to restore service while you investigate?

Devin (Acme Product): yes please apply something small (like 100k tokens) to get us through the day. also would love to know how to avoid this in future — can we get proactive alerts?

Maya (Support): done — i created a one-off credit (100000 tokens) and pushed it to your account at 2026-03-12T09:02:08Z. you should see service recovery now. for proactive alerts: enable usage webhooks in Console -> Alerts, or we can configure a threshold email/SMS at 80% and 95% usage. we can also enable an overage toggle (charges will apply) or a soft-fallback policy that routes to a smaller model automatically to avoid hard 429s.

Anika (SE): additional recommendations: 1) enable token-based webhooks so you get a POST to your endpoint when usage crosses thresholds; 2) configure model-fallback policies in the deployment to route to a cheaper quantized model when budget is low; 3) for high variance workloads, configure a buffer (reserve X% of monthly credits) and use forecasting from the Console Optimize tab — it predicts month-end spend given current rate.

Devin (Acme Product): great, thanks. one last question — if we have an account that resets on day 12, and we do a heavy spike at 23:59 UTC which completes at 00:01 UTC (two minutes into next cycle), which month is charged?

Maya (Support): it’s charged to the billing window where the request finalizes (charged_at). in your example it would charge to the new month's bucket because finalization_time is 00:01 UTC. if you need different semantics (e.g., charge by start_time) we can discuss enterprise billing customization, but the default is completion-time accounting.

Devin (Acme Product): understood — that explains our case. can you attach the request_ids for the big run so we can audit?

Maya (Support): sending the IDs to your email (devin@acme.com) now and adding Tom from Billing on thread. if you want, i can also open a short incident to update the dashboard wording re: completion-time billing so other customers aren’t confused.

ops-bot: deploy:analytics-dashboard v2.4.1 promoted to prod by ci-user at 2026-03-12T09:25:11Z :rocket:

Tom (Billing): note — billing will send a follow-up invoice amendment if the one-off credit affects month totals. i’ll CC billing-team@redwood.com on the email chain.

Devin (Acme Product): perfect, appreciate the fast help everyone :thumbsup:

Maya (Support): glad that helped. filing a small docs tweak ticket and enabling the 80/95% alerts for your account now. we’ll keep this open until you confirm recovery and receipts.

(End of thread)
